fluff.name: Monk
entries: Specialized warriors defined by their unique combat style and their reserve of internal power called ki. They use this ki to empower their attacks, bolster their defense, and create spell-like effects.

weapons: Martial weapons that have the Light property
tools: Choose one type of Artisan's Tools or Musical Instrument

entries: {@i Choose A or B:} (A) {@item Spear}, 5 {@item Dagger|Daggers}, {@item Artisan's Tools} or {@item Musical Instrument} chosen for the tool proficiency above, {@item Explorer's Pack}, and 11 GP; or (B) 50 GP

classFeature.name: Martial Arts
entries: Your practice of martial arts gives you mastery of combat styles that use your {@rule Unarmed Strike} and Monk weapons, which are the following:

items: Martial Melee Weapons that have the Light property

entries: You gain the following benefits while you are unarmed or wielding only Monk weapons and you aren't wearing armor or wielding a {@item Shield}.

entries.name: Bonus Unarmed Strike
entries: You can make an {@rule Unarmed Strike} as a {@rule Bonus Action}.

entries.name: Martial Arts Die
entries: You can roll {@damage 1d6} in place of the normal damage of your {@rule Unarmed Strike} or Monk weapons. This die changes as you gain Monk levels, as shown in the Martial Arts column of the Monk Features table.

entries.name: Dexterous Attacks
entries: You can use your Dexterity modifier instead of your Strength modifier for the attack and damage rolls of your Unarmed Strikes and Monk weapons. In addition, when you use the Grapple or Shove option of your {@rule Unarmed Strike}, you can use your Dexterity modifier instead of your Strength modifier to determine the save DC.

classFeature.name: Unarmored Defense
entries: While you aren't wearing armor or wielding a {@item Shield}, your base {@rule Armor Class} equals 10 plus your Dexterity and Wisdom modifiers.

classFeature.name: Monk's Focus
entries: Your focus and martial training allow you to harness a well of extraordinary energy within yourself. This energy is represented by Focus Points. Your Monk level determines the number of points you have, as shown in the Focus Points column of the Monk Features table.
You can expend these points to enhance or fuel certain Monk features. You start knowing three such features: Flurry of Blows, Patient Defense, and Step of the Wind, each of which is detailed below.
When you expend a Focus Point, it is unavailable until you finish a {@rule Short Rest|Short} or {@rule Long Rest}, at the end of which you regain all your expended points.
Some features that use Focus Points require your target to make a saving throw. The save DC equals 8 plus your Wisdom modifier and {@rule Proficiency|Proficiency Bonus}.

entries.name: Flurry of Blows
entries: You can expend 1 Focus Point to make two Unarmed Strikes as a {@rule Bonus Action}.

entries.name: Patient Defense
entries: You can take the {@action Disengage} action as a {@rule Bonus Action}. Alternatively, you can expend 1 Focus Point to take both the {@action Disengage} and the {@action Dodge} actions as a {@rule Bonus Action}.

entries.name: Step of the Wind
entries: You can take the {@action Dash} action as a {@rule Bonus Action}. Alternatively, you can expend 1 Focus Point to take both the {@action Disengage} and {@action Dash} actions as a {@rule Bonus Action}, and your jump distance is doubled for the turn.

classFeature.name: Unarmored Movement
entries: Your speed increases by 10 feet while you aren't wearing armor or wielding a {@item Shield}. This bonus increases when you reach certain Monk levels, as shown on the Monk Features table.

classFeature.name: Uncanny Metabolism
entries: When you roll {@rule Initiative}, you can regain all expended Focus Points. When you do so, roll your Martial Arts die, and regain a number of {@rule Hit Points} equal to your Monk level plus the number rolled.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@rule Long Rest}.

classFeature.name: Deflect Attacks
entries: When an attack roll hits you and its damage includes Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, you can take a {@rule Reaction} to reduce the attack's total damage against you. The reduction equals {@dice 1d10} plus your Dexterity modifier and Monk level.

If you reduce the damage to 0, you can expend 1 Focus Point to redirect some of the attack's force. If you do so, choose a creature you can see within 5 feet of yourself if the attack was a melee attack or a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself that isn't behind {@rule Cover|Total Cover} if the attack was a ranged attack. That creature must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take damage equal to two rolls of your Martial Arts die plus your Dexterity modifier. The damage is the same type dealt by the attack.

classFeature.name: Monk Subclass
entries: You gain a Monk subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Monk levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Monk level or lower.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement} feat or another {@feat |feat} of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Monk levels 8, 12, and 16.

classFeature.name: Slow Fall
entries: You can take a {@rule Reaction} when you fall to reduce any damage you take from the fall by an amount equal to five times your Monk level.

classFeature.name: Extra Attack
entries: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the {@action Attack} action on your turn.

classFeature.name: Stunning Strike
entries: Once per turn when you hit a creature with a Monk weapon or an {@rule Unarmed Strike}, you can expend 1 Focus Point to attempt a stunning strike. The target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the target has the {@condition Stunned} condition until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, the target's {@rule Speed} is halved until the start of your next turn, and the next attack roll made against the target before then has {@rule Advantage}.

classFeature.name: Empowered Strikes
entries: Whenever you deal damage with your {@rule Unarmed Strike}, it can deal your choice of Force damage or its normal damage type.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Monk subclass.

classFeature.name: Evasion
entries: When you're subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw and only half damage if you fail.
You don't benefit from this feature if you have the {@condition Incapacitated} condition.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement} feat or another {@feat |feat} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Acrobatic Movement
entries: While you aren't wearing armor or wielding a {@item Shield}, you gain the ability to move along vertical surfaces and across liquids on your turn without falling during the movement.

classFeature.name: Heightened Focus
entries: Your Flurry of Blows, Patient Defense, and Step of the Wind gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Flurry of Blows
entries: You can expend 1 Focus Point to use Flurry of Blows and make three Unarmed Strikes with it instead of two.

entries.name: Patient Defense
entries: When you expend a Focus Point to use Patient Defense, you gain a number of {@rule Temporary Hit Points} equal to two rolls of your Martial Arts die.

entries.name: Step of the Wind
entries: When you expend a Focus Point to use Step of the Wind, you can choose a willing creature within 5 feet of yourself that is Large or smaller. You move the creature with you until the end of your turn. The creature's movement doesn't provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|Opportunity Attacks}.

classFeature.name: Self-Restoration
entries: Through sheer force of will, you can remove one of the following conditions from yourself at the end of each of your turns: {@condition Charmed}, {@condition Frightened}, or {@condition Poisoned}.
In addition, forgoing food and drink doesn't give you levels of {@condition Exhaustion}.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Monk subclass.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement} feat or another {@feat |feat} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Deflect Energy
entries: You can now use your Deflect Attacks feature against attacks that deal any damage type, not just Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing.

classFeature.name: Disciplined Survivor
entries: Your physical and mental discipline grant you proficiency in all saving throws.
Additionally, whenever you make a saving throw and fail, you can expend 1 Focus Point to reroll it, and you must use the new roll.

classFeature.name: Perfect Focus
entries: When you roll {@rule Initiative} and don't use Uncanny Metabolism, you regain expended Focus Points until you have 4 if you have 3 or fewer.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement} feat or another {@feat |feat} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Monk subclass.

classFeature.name: Superior Defense
entries: At the start of your turn, you can expend 3 Focus Points to bolster yourself against harm for 1 minute or until you have the {@condition Incapacitated} condition. During that time, you have {@rule Resistance} to all damage except Force damage.

classFeature.name: Epic Boon
entries: You gain an {@epic-boon |Epic Boon feat} or another {@feat |feat} of your choice for which you qualify. {@epic-boon Boon of Irresistible Offense} is recommended.

classFeature.name: Body and Mind
entries: You have developed your body and mind to new heights. Your Dexterity and Wisdom scores increase by 4, to a maximum of 25.

subclassFeature.name: Warrior of Mercy
entries: {@i Manipulate Forces of Life and Death}

Warriors of Mercy manipulate the life force of others. These Monks are wandering physicians, but they bring a swift end to their enemies. They often wear masks, presenting themselves as faceless bringers of life and death.

subclassFeature.name: Hand of Harm
entries: Once per turn when you hit a creature with an {@rule Unarmed Strike} and deal damage, you can expend 1 Focus Point to deal extra Necrotic damage equal to one roll of your Martial Arts die plus your Wisdom modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Hand of Healing
entries: As a {@action Magic} action, you can expend 1 Focus Point to touch a creature and restore a number of {@rule Hit Points} equal to a roll of your Martial Arts die plus your Wisdom modifier. When you use your Flurry of Blows, you can replace one of the Unarmed Strikes with a use of this feature without expending a Focus Point for the healing.

subclassFeature.name: Implements of Mercy
entries: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Insight} and {@skill Medicine} skills and proficiency with the {@item Herbalism Kit}.

subclassFeature.name: Physician's Touch
entries: Your Hand of Harm and Hand of Healing improve, as detailed below.

entries.name: Hand of Harm
entries: When you use Hand of Harm on a creature, you can also give that creature the {@condition Poisoned} condition until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Hand of Healing
entries: When you use Hand of Healing, you can also end one of the following conditions on the creature you heal: {@condition Blinded}, {@condition Deafened}, {@condition Paralyzed}, {@condition Poisoned}, or {@condition Stunned}.

subclassFeature.name: Flurry of Healing and Harm
entries: When you use Flurry of Blows, you can replace each of the Unarmed Strikes with a use of Hand of Healing without expending Focus Points for the healing.

In addition, when you make an {@rule Unarmed Strike} with Flurry of Blows and deal damage, you can use Hand of Harm with that strike without expending a Focus Point for Hand of Harm. You can still use Hand of Harm only once per turn.
You can use these benefits a total number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@rule Long Rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Hand of Ultimate Mercy
entries: Your mastery of life energy opens the door to the ultimate mercy. As a {@action Magic} action, you can touch the corpse of a creature that died within the past 24 hours and expend 5 Focus Points. The creature then returns to life with a number of {@rule Hit Points} equal to {@dice 4d10} plus your Wisdom modifier. If the creature died with any of the following conditions, the creature revives with the conditions removed: {@condition Blinded}, {@condition Deafened}, {@condition Paralyzed}, {@condition Poisoned}, and {@condition Stunned}.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@rule Long Rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Warrior of Mystic Brews
entries: {@i Drink Mystic Brews to Overwhelm and Confound Foes}

Warriors of Mystic Brews move with the jerky, unpredictable movements typical of someone who is intoxicated. Their apparently erratic stumbles conceal a carefully executed dance of blocks, parries, advances, attacks, and retreats. Warriors of Mystic Brews frequent bars and taverns to gather information or spy on potential threats. These warriors drink magical concoctions that enhance their martial arts.
Warriors of Mystic Brews often enjoy playing the fool to bring gladness to the downtrodden or to teach humility to the arrogant, but these Monks are maddening, masterful foes in battle.

subclassFeature.name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Performance} skill, or if you already have it, you gain proficiency in one skill of your choice from the skills available to Monks at level 1. You also gain proficiency with {@item Brewer's Supplies} if you don't already have it.

subclassFeature.name: Drunken Technique
entries: You twist and turn quickly as you move. Whenever you expend a Monk's Focus using Patient Defense, your {@rule Speed} increases by 10 feet until the end of the current turn, and you can make one {@rule Unarmed Strike} immediately after the {@rule Bonus Action}.

subclassFeature.name: Tipsy Sway
entries: You can move in sudden, swaying ways. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Leap to Your Feet
entries: When you have the {@condition Prone} condition, you can stand up by spending 5 feet of movement.

entries.name: Redirect Attack
entries: When an enemy misses you with a melee attack roll, you can take a {@rule Reaction} and spend 1 Monk's Focus to cause that attack to hit one creature of your choice, other than the attacker, that you can see within 5 feet of yourself.

subclassFeature.name: Mystic Brew
entries: Whenever you finish a {@rule Short Rest|Short} or {@rule Long Rest} while holding {@item Brewer's Supplies}, you can use that tool to magically produce one magical beverage, chosen from the following options: Cinnamon Dragon, Heavenly Spirit, or Refreshing Dip. A pint of the beverage appears in a bottle or flask you are holding or carrying; otherwise, the beverage spills out on the ground and then vanishes. If any beverage remains when you finish a {@rule Short Rest|Short} or {@rule Long Rest}, the beverage vanishes.

entries.name: Drinking a Magical Beverage
entries: Only you can gain the benefits of drinking the beverage. You must drink the full pint of the beverage before gaining its benefit. You can spend 1 minute drinking the beverage. You then gain the benefits of the beverage for 1 hour or until you drink another magical beverage, as described below:

items.name: Cinnamon Dragon
items.entry: You can take a {@action Magic} action to exhale toxic flames in a 30-foot {@rule Cone [Area of Effect]|Cone}. Each creature in the {@rule Cone [Area of Effect]|Cone} makes a Dexterity saving throw ({@dc 8} plus your Wisdom modifier and {@rule Proficiency|Proficiency Bonus}). On a failed save, a creature takes Fire damage equal to four rolls of your Martial Arts die and has the {@condition Poisoned} condition until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage only.

items.name: Heavenly Spirit
items.entry: You gain {@rule Resistance} to two of the following damage types of your choice: Cold, Necrotic, Psychic, or Radiant damage.

items.name: Refreshing Dip
items.entry: You have a pool of dice of the same type as your Martial Arts die. The maximum number of dice equals your Wisdom modifier plus half your Monk level (round down). Whenever you regain {@rule Hit Points}, you can expend and roll one die from this pool to regain additional {@rule Hit Points} equal to the number rolled.

entries.name: Enhancing a Magical Beverage
entries: When you create a magical beverage, you can expend 1 Monk's Focus to extend the benefits' duration to 8 hours.

subclassFeature.name: Wizened Brewer
entries: You learn more complex flavors. The following beverages are added to your Mystic Brew options:

items.name: Blue Lightning
items.entry: Whenever you take a {@rule Reaction} that isn't making an {@action Opportunity Attack} or casting a spell, you can make one {@rule Unarmed Strike} as part of that {@rule Reaction}.

items.name: Drunkard's Luck
items.entry: You gain {@rule Heroic Inspiration} if you don't already have it. In addition, you can give yourself {@rule Heroic Inspiration} when you make an ability check or saving throw without it.

items.name: Stumbling Monk
items.entry: When you take a {@rule Bonus Action} other than Patient Defense, you can also use Patient Defense immediately after that {@rule Bonus Action}.

subclassFeature.name: Master Brewer
entries: When you create a magical beverage using your Mystic Brew feature, you can choose two different options and produce one magical beverage. Drinking the beverage provides the effects of both options for the duration.

subclassFeature.name: Intoxicated Frenzy
entries: Immediately after you use your Patient Defense, you can move up to your {@rule Speed}. During this movement, whenever you enter a space within 5 feet of a creature, you can make an {@rule Unarmed Strike} targeting that creature. In addition, when you hit a creature with an {@rule Unarmed Strike} granted by this feature, the creature must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or have the {@condition Prone} condition. A creature can be targeted by an {@rule Unarmed Strike} granted by this feature only once per turn.

subclassFeature.name: Warrior of Shadow
entries: {@i Harness Shadow Power for Stealth and Subterfuge}

Warriors of Shadow practice stealth and subterfuge, harnessing the power of the Shadowfell. They are at home in darkness, able to draw gloom around themselves to hide, leap from shadow to shadow, and take on a wraithlike form.

subclassFeature.name: Shadow Arts
entries: You have learned to draw on the power of the Shadowfell, gaining the following benefits.

entries.name: Darkness
entries: You can expend 1 Focus Point to cast the {@spell Darkness} spell without spell components. You can see within the spell's area when you cast it with this feature. While the spell persists, you can move its area of {@rule Darkness} to a space within 60 feet of yourself at the start of each of your turns.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You gain {@sense Darkvision} with a range of 60 feet. If you already have {@sense Darkvision}, its range increases by 60 feet.

entries.name: Shadowy Figments
entries: You know the {@spell Minor Illusion} spell. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for it.

subclassFeature.name: Shadow Step
entries: While entirely within {@rule Dim Light} or {@rule Darkness}, you can use a {@rule Bonus Action} to teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see that is also in {@rule Dim Light} or {@rule Darkness}. You then have {@rule Advantage} on the next melee attack you make before the end of the current turn.

subclassFeature.name: Improved Shadow Step
entries: You can draw on your Shadowfell connection to empower your teleportation. When you use your Shadow Step, you can expend 1 Focus Point to remove the requirement that you must start and end in {@rule Dim Light} or {@rule Darkness} for that use of the feature. As part of this {@rule Bonus Action}, you can make an {@rule Unarmed Strike} immediately after you teleport.

subclassFeature.name: Cloak of Shadows
entries: As a {@action Magic} action while entirely within {@rule Dim Light} or {@rule Darkness}, you can expend 3 Focus Points to shroud yourself with shadows for 1 minute, until you have the {@condition Incapacitated} condition, or until you end your turn in {@rule Bright Light}. While shrouded by these shadows, you gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Invisibility
entries: You have the {@condition Invisible} condition.

entries.name: Partially Incorporeal
entries: You can move through occupied spaces as if they were {@rule Difficult Terrain}. If you end your turn in such a space, you are shunted to the last unoccupied space you were in.

entries.name: Shadow Flurry
entries: You can use your Flurry of Blows without expending any Focus Points.

subclassFeature.name: Warrior of the Elements
entries: {@i Wield Strikes and Bursts of Elemental Power}

Warriors of the Elements tap into the power of the Elemental Planes. Harnessing their supernatural focus, these Monks momentarily tame the energy of the Elemental Chaos to empower themselves in and out of battle.

subclassFeature.name: Elemental Attunement
entries: At the start of your turn, you can expend 1 Focus Point to imbue yourself with elemental energy. The energy lasts for 10 minutes or until you have the {@condition Incapacitated} condition. You gain the following benefits while this feature is active.

entries.name: Reach
entries: When you make an {@rule Unarmed Strike}, your reach is 10 feet greater than normal, as elemental energy extends from you.

entries.name: Elemental Strikes
entries: Whenever you hit with your {@rule Unarmed Strike}, you can cause it to deal your choice of Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder damage rather than its normal damage type. When you deal one of these types with it, you can also force the target to make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, you can move the target up to 10 feet toward or away from you, as elemental energy swirls around it.

subclassFeature.name: Manipulate Elements
entries: You know the {@spell Elementalism} spell. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for it.

subclassFeature.name: Elemental Burst
entries: As a {@action Magic} action, you can expend 2 Focus Points to cause elemental energy to burst in a 20-foot-radius {@rule Sphere [Area of Effect]|Sphere} centered on a point within 120 feet of yourself. Choose a damage type: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder.

Each creature in the {@rule Sphere [Area of Effect]|Sphere} must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes damage of the chosen type equal to three rolls of your Martial Arts die. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage.

subclassFeature.name: Stride of the Elements
entries: While your Elemental Attunement is active, you also have a {@rule Fly Speed} and a {@rule Swim Speed} equal to your {@rule Speed}.

subclassFeature.name: Elemental Epitome
entries: While your Elemental Attunement is active, you also gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Damage Resistance
entries: You gain {@rule Resistance} to one of the following damage types of your choice: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder. At the start of each of your turns, you can change this choice.

entries.name: Destructive Stride
entries: When you use your Step of the Wind, your {@rule Speed} increases by 20 feet until the end of the turn. For that duration, any creature of your choice takes damage equal to one roll of your Martial Arts die when you enter a space within 5 feet of it. The damage type is your choice of Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder. A creature can take this damage only once per turn.

entries.name: Empowered Strikes
entries: Once on each of your turns, you can deal extra damage to a target equal to one roll of your Martial Arts die when you hit it with an {@rule Unarmed Strike}. The extra damage is the same type dealt by that strike.

subclassFeature.name: Warrior of the Mystic Arts
entries: {@i Weave Martial and Mystic Arts}
Warriors of the Mystic Arts wield magic to supplement their martial skill. They harness mystical focus to enhance their magical and physical abilities.

subclassFeature.name: Spellcasting
entries: You have learned to cast spells. See the Player's Handbook for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules as a Warrior of the Mystic Arts.

entries.name: Cantrips
entries: You know two cantrips of your choice from the Sorcerer spell list. {@spell Blade Ward} and {@spell Thunderclap} are recommended. Whenever you gain a Monk level, you can replace one of these cantrips with another cantrip of your choice from the Sorcerer spell list.
When you reach Monk level 10, you learn another Sorcerer cantrip of your choice.

entries.name: Spell Slots
entries: The Warrior of the Mystic Arts Spellcasting table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a {@rule Long Rest}.

entries.name: Prepared Spells of Level 1+
entries: You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose three level 1 spells from the Sorcerer spell list. {@spell Jump}, {@spell Magic Missile}, and {@spell Shield} are recommended.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Monk levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Warrior of the Mystic Arts Spellcasting table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional spells from the Sorcerer spell list until the number of spells on your list matches the number on the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 7 Monk, your list of prepared spells can include five Sorcerer spells of levels 1 and 2 in any combination.

entries.name: Changing Your Prepared Spells
entries: Whenever you gain a Monk level, you can replace one spell on your list with another Sorcerer spell for which you have spell slots.

entries.name: Spellcasting Ability
entries: Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your Sorcerer spells.

entries.name: Spellcasting Focus
entries: You can use an {@item Arcane Focus} as a {@rule Spellcasting Focus} for your Sorcerer spells.

entries.name: Multiclassing
entries: If you multiclass and have the Spellcasting feature from more than one class, add one third of your Monk levels (round down) to determine your available spell slots.

subclassFeature.name: Mystic Fighting Style
entries: When you take the {@action Attack} action on your turn, you can replace one {@rule Unarmed Strike} with a casting of one of your Sorcerer cantrips that has a casting time of an action.

subclassFeature.name: Mystic Focus
entries: You keep your magical power and martial focus in perfect balance, allowing you to convert spell slots into Focus Points, or convert Focus Points into spell slots.

entries.name: Converting Spell Slots to Focus Points
entries: You can expend a spell slot to regain a number of expended Focus Points equal to the slot's level (no action required).

entries.name: Recovering Spell Slots
entries: When you finish a {@rule Short Rest} or use Uncanny Metabolism, you can transform unexpended Focus Points to recover one expended spell slot. The Recovering Spell Slots table shows the cost of recovering a spell slot of a given level, and it lists the minimum Monk level you must be to recover a slot. You can recover a spell slot no higher than level 4.

subclassFeature.name: Focused Strike
entries: When you use your Stunning Strike, whether the target succeeds or fails on the saving throw, the target has {@rule Disadvantage} on saving throws against your spells until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Improved Mystic Fighting Style
entries: When you use Flurry of Blows, you can replace two of the {@rule Unarmed Strike|Unarmed Strikes} with a casting of one of your level 1 or 2 Sorcerer spells that has a casting time of an action, and you cast it as part of the same {@rule Bonus Action} you use to activate Flurry of Blows.

subclassFeature.name: Warrior of the Open Hand
entries: {@i Master Unarmed Combat Techniques}
Warriors of the Open Hand are masters of unarmed combat. They learn techniques to push and trip their opponents and manipulate their own energy to protect themselves from harm.

subclassFeature.name: Open Hand Technique
entries: Whenever you hit a creature with an attack granted by your Flurry of Blows, you can impose one of the following effects on that target.

entries.name: Addle
entries: The target can't make {@action Opportunity Attack|Opportunity Attacks} until the start of its next turn.

entries.name: Push
entries: The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be pushed up to 15 feet away from you.

entries.name: Topple
entries: The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or have the {@condition Prone} condition.

subclassFeature.name: Wholeness of Body
entries: You gain the ability to heal yourself. As a {@rule Bonus Action}, you can roll your Martial Arts die. You regain a number of {@rule Hit Points} equal to the number rolled plus your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1 {@rule Hit Points|Hit Point} regained).
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@rule Long Rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Fleet Step
entries: When you take a {@rule Bonus Action} other than Step of the Wind, you can also use Step of the Wind immediately after that {@rule Bonus Action}.

subclassFeature.name: Quivering Palm
entries: You gain the ability to set up lethal vibrations in someone's body. When you hit a creature with an {@rule Unarmed Strike}, you can expend 4 Focus Points to start these imperceptible vibrations, which last for a number of days equal to your Monk level. The vibrations are harmless unless you take an action to end them. Alternatively, when you take the {@action Attack} action on your turn, you can forgo one of the attacks to end the vibrations. To end them, you and the target must be on the same plane of existence. When you end them, the target must make a Constitution saving throw, taking {@damage 10d12} Force damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.
You can have only one creature under the effect of this feature at a time. You can end the vibrations harmlessly (no action required).

subclassFeature.name: Way of the Ascendant Dragon
entries: The dragon god Bahamut is known to travel the Material Plane in the guise of a young monk, and legend says that he founded the first monastery of the Way of the Ascendant Dragon in this guise. The fundamental teaching of this tradition holds that by emulating dragons, a monk becomes a more integrated part of the world and its magic. By altering their spirit to resonate with draconic might, monks who follow this tradition augment their prowess in battle, bolster their allies, and can even soar through the air on draconic wings. But all this power is in service of a greater goal: achieving a spiritual unity with the essence of the Material Plane.
As a follower of the Way of the Ascendant Dragon, you decide how you unlocked the power of dragons within yourself. The Ascendant Dragon Origin table offers a number of possibilities.

entries.caption: Ascendant Dragon Origin
rows: You honed your abilities by aligning your spirit with a dragon's world-altering power.
A dragon personally took an active role in shaping your inner energy.
You studied at a monastery that traces its teachings back centuries or more to a single dragon's instruction, or one that is devoted to a dragon god.
You spent long stretches meditating in the region around an ancient dragon's lair, absorbing that lair's ambient magic.
You found a scroll written in Draconic that contained inspiring new techniques.
After a dream featuring a five-handed dragonborn, you awoke with the mystical breath of dragons.

subclassFeature.name: Draconic Disciple
entries: {@i 3rd-level Way of the Ascendant Dragon feature}
You can channel draconic power to magnify your presence and imbue your unarmed strikes with the essence of a dragon's breath. You gain the following benefits:

items.name: Draconic Presence
items.entry: If you fail a Charisma ({@skill Intimidation}) or Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) check, you can use your reaction to reroll the check, as you tap into the mighty presence of dragons. Once this feature turns a failure into a success, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

items.name: Draconic Strike
items.entry: When you damage a target with an unarmed strike, you can change the damage type to acid, cold, fire, lightning, or poison.

items.name: Tongue of Dragons
items.entry: You learn to speak, read, and write {@language Draconic} or one other language of your choice.

subclassFeature.name: Breath of the Dragon
entries: {@i 3rd-level Way of the Ascendant Dragon feature}

You can channel destructive waves of energy, like those created by the dragons you emulate. When you take the {@action Attack} action on your turn, you can replace one of the attacks with an exhalation of draconic energy in either a 20-foot cone or a 30-foot line that is 5 feet wide (your choice). Choose a damage type: acid, cold, fire, lightning, or poison. Each creature in that area must make a Dexterity saving throw against your ki save DC, taking damage of the chosen type equal to two rolls of your Martial Arts die on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
At 11th level, the damage of this feature increases to three rolls of your Martial Arts die.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest. While you have no uses available, you can spend 2 ki points to use this feature again.

subclassFeature.name: Wings Unfurled
entries: {@i 6th-level Way of the Ascendant Dragon feature}

When you use your Step of the Wind, you can unfurl spectral draconic wings from your back that vanish at the end of your turn. While the wings exist, you have a flying speed equal to your walking speed.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Aspect of the Wyrm
entries: {@i 11th-level Way of the Ascendant Dragon feature}

The power of your draconic spirit now radiates from you, warding your allies or inspiring fear in your enemies. As a bonus action, you can create an aura of draconic power that radiates 10 feet from you for 1 minute. For the duration, you gain one of the following effects of your choice:

items.name: Frightful Presence
items.entry: When you create this aura, and as a bonus action on subsequent turns, you can choose a creature within the aura. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your ki save DC or become {@condition frightened} of you for 1 minute. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a successful save.

items.name: Resistance
items.entry: Choose a damage type when you activate this aura: acid, cold, fire, lightning, or poison. You and your allies within the aura have resistance to that damage.

entries: Once you create this aura, you can't create it again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend 3 ki points to create it again.

subclassFeature.name: Ascendant Aspect
entries: {@i 17th-level Way of the Ascendant Dragon feature}
Your draconic spirit reaches its peak. You gain the following benefits:

items.name: Augment Breath
items.entry: When you use your Breath of the Dragon, you can spend 1 ki point to augment its shape and power. The exhalation of draconic energy becomes either a 60-foot cone or a 90-foot line that is 5 feet wide (your choice), and each creature in that area takes damage equal to four rolls of your Martial Arts die on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

items.name: Blindsight
items.entry: You gain {@sense blindsight} out to 10 feet. Within that range, you can effectively see anything that isn't behind total cover, even if you're {@condition blinded} or in darkness. Moreover, you can see an {@condition invisible} creature within that range, unless the creature successfully hides from you.

items.name: Explosive Fury
items.entry: When you activate your Aspect of the Wyrm, draconic fury explodes from you. Choose any number of creatures you can see in your aura. Each of those creatures must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw against your ki save DC or take {@damage 3d10} acid, cold, fire, lightning, or poison damage (your choice).

subclassFeature.name: Way of the Astral Self
entries: A monk who follows the Way of the Astral Self believes their body is an illusion. They see their ki as a representation of their true form, an astral self. This astral self has the capacity to be a force of order or disorder, with some monasteries training students to use their power to protect the weak and other instructing aspirants in how to manifest their true selves in service to the mighty.

subclassFeature.name: Forms of Your Astral Self
entries: The astral self is a translucent embodiment of the monk's soul. As a result, an astral self can reflect aspects of a monk's background, ideals, flaws, and bonds, and an astral self doesn't necessarily look anything like the monk. For example, the astral self of a lanky human might be reminiscent of a minotaur-the strength of which the monk feels within. Similarly, an orc monk might manifest gossamer arms and a delicate visage, representing the gentle beauty of the orc's soul. Each astral self is unique, and some of the monks of this monastic tradition are known more for the appearance of their astral self than for their physical appearance.

When choosing this path, consider the quirks that define your monk. Are you obsessed with something? Are you driven by justice or a selfish desire? Any of these motivations could manifest in the form of your astral self.

subclassFeature.name: Arms of the Astral Self
entries: {@i 3rd-level Way of the Astral Self feature}

Your mastery of your ki allows you to summon a portion of your astral self. As a bonus action, you can spend 1 ki point to summon the arms of your astral self. When you do so, each creature of your choice that you can see within 10 feet of you must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take force damage equal to two rolls of your Martial Arts die.

For 10 minutes, these spectral arms hover near your shoulders or surround your arms (your choice). You determine the arms' appearance, and they vanish early if you are {@condition incapacitated} or die.
While the spectral arms are present, you gain the following benefits:

items: You can use your Wisdom modifier in place of your Strength modifier when making Strength checks and Strength saving throws.
You can use the spectral arms to make unarmed strikes.
When you make an unarmed strike with the arms on your turn, your reach for it is 5 feet greater than normal.
The unarmed strikes you make with the arms can use your Wisdom modifier in place of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls, and their damage type is force.

subclassFeature.name: Visage of the Astral Self
entries: {@i 6th-level Way of the Astral Self feature}

You can summon the visage of your astral self. As a bonus action, or as part of the bonus action you take to activate Arms of the Astral Self, you can spend 1 ki point to summon this visage for 10 minutes. It vanishes early if you are {@condition incapacitated} or die.
The spectral visage covers your face like a helmet or mask. You determine its appearance.
While the spectral visage is present, you gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Astral Sight
entries: You can see normally in darkness, both magical and nonmagical, to a distance of 120 feet.

entries.name: Wisdom of the Spirit
entries: You have advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) and Charisma ({@skill Intimidation}) checks.

entries.name: Word of the Spirit
entries: When you speak, you can direct your words to a creature of your choice that you can see within 60 feet of you, making it so only that creature can hear you. Alternatively, you can amplify your voice so that all creatures within 600 feet can hear you.

subclassFeature.name: Body of the Astral Self
entries: {@i 11th-level Way of the Astral Self feature}

When you have both your astral arms and visage summoned, you can cause the body of your astral self to appear (no action required). This spectral body covers your physical form like a suit of armor, connecting with the arms and visage. You determine its appearance.
While the spectral body is present, you gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Deflect Energy
entries: When you take acid, cold, fire, force, lightning, or thunder damage, you can use your reaction to deflect it. When you do so, the damage you take is reduced by {@dice 1d10} + your Wisdom modifier (minimum reduction of 1).

entries.name: Empowered Arms
entries: Once on each of your turns when you hit a target with the Arms of the Astral Self, you can deal extra damage to the target equal to your Martial Arts die.

subclassFeature.name: Awakened Astral Self
entries: {@i 17th-level Way of the Astral Self feature}

Your connection to your astral self is complete, allowing you to unleash its full potential. As a bonus action, you can spend 5 ki points to summon the arms, visage, and body of your astral self and awaken it for 10 minutes. This awakening ends early if you are {@condition incapacitated} or die.
While your astral self is awakened, you gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Armor of the Spirit
entries: You gain a +2 bonus to Armor Class.

entries.name: Astral Barrage
entries: Whenever you use the Extra Attack feature to attack twice, you can instead attack three times if all the attacks are made with your astral arms.

subclassFeature.name: Way of the Kensei
entries: Monks of the Way of the Kensei train relentlessly with their weapons, to the point where the weapon becomes an extension of the body. Founded on a mastery of sword fighting, the tradition has expanded to include many different weapons.

A kensei sees a weapon in much the same way a calligrapher or painter regards a pen or brush. Whatever the weapon, the kensei views it as a tool used to express the beauty and precision of the martial arts. That such mastery makes a kensei a peerless warrior is but a side effect of intense devotion, practice, and study.

subclassFeature.name: Path of the Kensei
entries: When you choose this tradition at 3rd level, your special martial arts training leads you to master the use of certain weapons. This path also includes instruction in the deft strokes of calligraphy or painting. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Kensei Weapons
entries: Choose two types of weapons to be your kensei weapons: one melee weapon and one ranged weapon. Each of these weapons can be any simple or martial weapon that lacks the heavy and special properties. The longbow is also a valid choice. You gain proficiency with these weapons if you don't already have it. Weapons of the chosen types are monk weapons for you. Many of this tradition's features work only with your kensei weapons. When you reach 6th, 11th, and 17th level in this class, you can choose another type of weapon—either melee or ranged—to be a kensei weapon for you, following the criteria above.

entries.name: Agile Parry
entries: If you make an unarmed strike as part of the {@action Attack} action on your turn and are holding a kensei weapon, you can use it to defend yourself if it is a melee weapon. You gain a +2 bonus to AC until the start of your next turn, while the weapon is in your hand and you aren't {@condition incapacitated}.

entries.name: Kensei's Shot
entries: You can use a bonus action on your turn to make your ranged attacks with a kensei weapon more deadly. When you do so, any target you hit with a ranged attack using a kensei weapon takes an extra {@damage 1d4} damage of the weapon's type. You retain this benefit until the end of the current turn.

entries.name: Way of the Brush
entries: You gain proficiency with your choice of {@item calligrapher's supplies} or {@item painter's supplies}.

subclassFeature.name: One with the Blade
entries: At 6th level, you extend your ki into your kensei weapons, granting you the following benefits.

entries.name: Magic Kensei Weapons
entries: Your attacks with your kensei weapons count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.

entries.name: Deft Strike
entries: When you hit a target with a kensei weapon, you can spend 1 ki point to cause the weapon to deal extra damage to the target equal to your Martial Arts die. You can use this feature only once on each of your turns.

subclassFeature.name: Sharpen the Blade
entries: At 11th level, you gain the ability to augment your weapons further with your ki. As a bonus action, you can expend up to 3 ki points to grant one kensei weapon you touch a bonus to attack and damage rolls when you attack with it. The bonus equals the number of ki points you spent. This bonus lasts for 1 minute or until you use this feature again. This feature has no effect on a magic weapon that already has a bonus to attack and damage rolls.

subclassFeature.name: Unerring Accuracy
entries: At 17th level, your mastery of weapons grants you extraordinary accuracy. If you miss with an attack roll using a monk weapon on your turn, you can reroll it. You can use this feature only once on each of your turns.

subclassFeature.name: Way of the Long Death
entries: Monks of the Way of the Long Death are obsessed with the meaning and mechanics of dying. They capture creatures and prepare elaborate experiments to capture, record, and understand the moments of their demise. They use this knowledge to guide their understanding of martial arts, yielding a deadly fighting style.

subclassFeature.name: Touch of Death
entries: Starting when you choose this tradition at 3rd level, your study of death allows you to extract vitality from another creature as it nears its demise. When you reduce a creature within 5 feet of you to 0 hit points, you gain temporary hit points equal to your Wisdom modifier + your monk level (minimum of 1 temporary hit point).

subclassFeature.name: Hour of Reaping
entries: At 6th level, you gain the ability to unsettle or terrify those around you as an action, for your soul has been touched by the shadow of death. When you take this action, each creature within 30 feet of you that can see you must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be {@condition frightened} of you until the end of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Mastery of Death
entries: Beginning at 11th level, you use your familiarity with death to escape its grasp. When you are reduced to 0 hit points, you can expend 1 ki point (no action required) to have 1 hit point instead.

subclassFeature.name: Touch of the Long Death
entries: Starting at 17th level, your touch can channel the energy of death into a creature. As an action, you touch one creature within 5 feet of you, and you expend 1 to 10 ki points. The target must make a Constitution saving throw, and it takes {@damage 2d10} necrotic damage per ki point spent on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

subclassFeature.name: Way of the Sun Soul
entries: Monks of the Way of the Sun Soul learn to channel their life energy into searing bolts of light. They teach that meditation can unlock the ability to unleash the indomitable light shed by the soul of every living creature.

subclassFeature.name: Radiant Sun Bolt
entries: Starting when you choose this tradition at 3rd level, you can hurl searing bolts of magical radiance.

You gain a new attack option that you can use with the {@action Attack} action. The special attack is a ranged spell attack with a range of 30 feet. You are proficient with it, and you add your Dexterity modifier to its attack and damage rolls. Its damage is radiant, and its damage die is a {@damage d4}. This die changes as you gain monk levels, as shown in the Martial Arts column of the Monk table.

When you take the {@action Attack} action on your turn and use this special attack as part of it, you can spend 1 ki point to make the special attack twice as a bonus action. When you gain the Extra Attack feature, this special attack can be used for any of the attacks you make as part of the {@action Attack} action.

subclassFeature.name: Searing Arc Strike
entries: At 6th level, you gain the ability to channel your ki into searing waves of energy. Immediately after you take the {@action Attack} action on your turn, you can spend 2 ki points to cast the {@spell burning hands} spell as a bonus action.

You can spend additional ki points to cast {@spell burning hands} as a higher-level spell. Each additional ki point you spend increases the spell's level by 1. The maximum number of ki points (2 plus any additional points) that you can spend on the spell equals half your monk level.

subclassFeature.name: Searing Sunburst
entries: At 11th level, you gain the ability to create an orb of light that erupts into a devastating explosion. As an action, you magically create an orb and hurl it at a point you choose within 150 feet, where it erupts into a sphere of radiant light for a brief but deadly instant.

Each creature in that 20-foot-radius sphere must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or take {@damage 2d6} radiant damage. A creature doesn't need to make the save if the creature is behind total cover that is opaque.
You can increase the sphere's damage by spending ki points. Each point you spend, to a maximum of 3, increases the damage by {@damage 2d6}.

subclassFeature.name: Sun Shield
entries: At 17th level, you become wreathed in a luminous, magical aura. You shed bright light in a 30-foot radius and dim light for an additional 30 feet. You can extinguish or restore the light as a bonus action.
If a creature hits you with a melee attack while this light shines, you can use your reaction to deal radiant damage to the creature. The radiant damage equals 5 + your Wisdom modifier.
